name: Pre-Launch Diagnostic Gate
hypothesis: A pre-launch diagnostic gate that validates subprocess readiness before each iteration will reduce pre-launch failures below 2% and overall failure rate below 3%.
change: In the orchestrator iteration path (orchestrator.go), before the Build stage is invoked, run a lightweight preflight diagnostic: (1) procutil.WaitForProcessCapacity with increased timeout, (2) provider binary existence check, (3) config/prompt render dry-run. If preflight fails, emit a typed 'prelaunch_blocked' reason with diagnostic details and skip the iteration with a short backoff, rather than recording a zero-attribution failure row.
measurement: Pre-launch failure rate (model='' AND duration_ms=0 iterations / total). Target: <2% (from 9.7% baseline). Secondary: overall failure rate target <3% (from 10.4% baseline), unknown-attribution rate target <2%.
risk: Adds ~100-200ms per iteration for preflight checks. Could mask real failures if diagnostic gate is too permissive. Backoff delays could slow throughput on transient capacity issues.

previous_experiment.name: Stream Event Matrix Gate Before Merge
previous_experiment.final_summary: Hypothesis not confirmed. 94 iterations: unknown attribution 10.6% (target <5%). All unknown-attribution rows were pre-launch invocation failures (model='', cost=$0, duration=0ms), not stream-event parsing failures. Attributed iterations showed 4.8% failure rate (better than baseline). Experiment targeted wrong root cause.
